docs.title: Prompt-level response cache keying
docs.purpose: the design for prompt-level response cache keying
docs.hint: Add a `cache_stats()` method to `curator.LLM` that reports how many of the last run's requests were served from the local cache versus sent to the backend, so users can gauge how much a re-run will cost before running it.

planted.text: Writing down what I think the sane behaviour is, because right now everyone's answer is rm -rf on the cache dir: if generation_params differ from the stored run, those rows should be going out to the provider again, and only those rows.
planted.settles: the team agrees differing generation_params should force a resend of just those rows

docs.author: dario
docs.title: Structured output schema validation before dispatch
docs.purpose: the design for structured output schema validation before dispatch
docs.hint: Before sending any request to a backend, validate that the `response_format` Pydantic model passed to `curator.LLM` is compatible with structured-output mode for the selected model, and fail early with a clear message if not.

planted.text: Adding this to the troubleshooting page since it is the third report: if you edit your response_format between runs, either wipe the cache directory or set CURATOR_DISABLE_CACHE=1 first, otherwise you will get objects built to the previous schema.
planted.settles: the team agrees a schema edit today requires manually discarding stored responses

docs.author: emil
docs.title: Batch job status persistence across process restarts
docs.purpose: the design for batch job status persistence across process restarts
docs.hint: Ensure that if a Python process running a `batch=True` job is killed and restarted while a batch job is still pending on the provider's side, re-running the same script resumes polling the existing batch job instead of submitting a duplicate one.

planted.text: House rule for anything that only reports on the cache: connect to the metadata db with mode=ro.
planted.settles: the team agrees reporting paths open the metadata db in ro mode and create nothing

threads.subject: Re: Prompt-level response cache keying
threads.purpose: working out prompt-level response cache keying over mail
threads.hint: Add a `cache_stats()` method to `curator.LLM` that reports how many of the last run's requests were served from the local cache versus sent to the backend, so users can gauge how much a re-run will cost before running it.

planted.text: Line I'd like us to actually hold to, since it keeps coming up in review. A cache write is an optimisation for the next run. Failing one makes the next run more expensive, it does not make this run invalid. So nothing that has already cost the user money gets aborted because we couldn't put a file on disk, we take the hit on the rerun and carry on.
planted.settles: the team agrees an already-billed operation must not be aborted by a failed cache write

threads.subject: Re: Structured output schema validation before dispatch
threads.purpose: working out structured output schema validation before dispatch over mail
threads.hint: Before sending any request to a backend, validate that the `response_format` Pydantic model passed to `curator.LLM` is compatible with structured-output mode for the selected model, and fail early with a clear message if not.

threads.subject: Re: Batch job status persistence across process restarts
threads.purpose: working out batch job status persistence across process restarts over mail
threads.hint: Ensure that if a Python process running a `batch=True` job is killed and restarted while a batch job is still pending on the provider's side, re-running the same script resumes polling the existing batch job instead of submitting a duplicate one.

planted.text: For what it's worth, the online processor appends to the responses file the moment a request is accepted, not when it comes back. That ordering was deliberate and we argued about it for a while.
planted.settles: the team agrees the house ordering is to record the accepted side effect before beginning to wait on it

planted.text: Support thread worth reading: user points CURATOR_CACHE_DIR at /mnt/shared so they can start a run on the laptop and finish it on the box. Their expectation is that everything a rerun needs is under that path. Today the request and response files follow CURATOR_CACHE_DIR and nothing else does, so "resumable" means two different things depending on which half of the run you're talking about, and they noticed.
planted.settles: the team agrees users expect everything needed for a rerun to live under CURATOR_CACHE_DIR

threads.subject: Re: Docker code executor image pinning
threads.purpose: working out docker code executor image pinning over mail
threads.hint: Pin the Docker image used by the Docker backend of `CodeExecutor` to a specific tag rather than `latest`, and allow callers to override it via `backend_params`.

planted.text: If we do tighten this, my preference is the first task blows up at create.
planted.settles: the team agrees an incompatible image should stop the run at container start rather than continue

planted.text: Reading the docker backend before I review this: when a caller sets `backend_params={'image': ...}` the create call goes down a shorter path than the default one, and the extra kwargs we assemble for our own tag never get near it. I do not think anybody chose that, it is just where the code ended up.
planted.settles: the team agrees the override path skips the container settings the default path applies

planted.text: On the thread with the team who want their own image: they want it purely so scipy and their internal client lib are already there, they are not asking us to change how the container runs. I told them the workspace still comes in read-only from our side and they said fine, they write everything to stdout anyway.
planted.settles: the team agrees a caller-supplied image is expected to keep the write-protected workspace
